_README: Literature H-diffusivity Arrhenius laws, consumed by diffusivity_plot.py.
Top-level keys are materials, named as in a paper ('316L SS', 'Hastelloy N',
'NiO'). A run folder finds its key by its name without the H count and
without the structure words '_supercell', '_bestsqs' and '_sqs': folder
'Al_supercell_10H' looks for 'Al', 'HastelloyN_bestsqs_5H' for 'Hastelloy N'.
Matching ignores case, spaces, underscores and hyphens. A run whose name
differs from its key in more than that (a typo, a seed number, 'oxide' for a
formula) is listed in _ALIASES: run-folder name -> key.
Any key starting with '_' is documentation (or the alias table) and is not
a material.
Each entry is drawn ONLY across its own T_C window - a study measured over
300-600 C is never extrapolated to meet the MD points.
A malformed entry is reported on stderr and dropped; the rest still plot.
Isotopes: every entry is drawn. A deuterium (D2) law carries a dagger (†) at
the end of its label and a tritium (T2) law an asterisk (*); hydrogen is
unmarked. The 'isotope' field says the same.
Laws read off a published figure (digitised) rather than printed carry
'digitised_from' with the figure, and their note gives the line's ends.
Units are the same for every entry: energies in kJ/mol, and D0 in the
units its schema names. A value printed in other units is converted and the
printed value kept in 'as_printed'; a law read off a figure is converted from
the reading.

_SCHEMA.label: REQUIRED. Citation as it should appear in the legend, e.g. 'Zhang et al. 2026'.
_SCHEMA.isotope: OPTIONAL. 'H2' (default), 'D2' or 'T2'. The label marks a D2 law with a dagger (†) and a T2 law with an asterisk (*).
_SCHEMA.D0: REQUIRED. Pre-exponential factor, as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.Ea: REQUIRED. Activation energy, as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.Ea_units: Units of Ea: always 'kJ/mol' in this file. A value printed in other units is converted, and the printed value is kept in 'as_printed'.
_SCHEMA.T_C: REQUIRED (or T_K). Validity range [low, high] in degrees Celsius; null when no range is known: the law is stored but not drawn.
_SCHEMA.T_K: Alternative to T_C: validity range [low, high] in Kelvin.
_SCHEMA.digitised_from: OPTIONAL. Set when the law was read off a published figure instead of printed: the figure it came from. Such laws are named as read off a figure in the plot caption.
_SCHEMA.as_printed: Set when a printed value was converted to this file's units: the value and unit as printed in the source.
_SCHEMA.note: OPTIONAL. Free-text provenance - method, purity, DOI. Not plotted.

Tanabe, Kinetics of Hydrogen in Metals, Springer Series in Materials Science 357 (Springer, 2026), Ch. 7, Table 7.2 (recommended values), doi:10.1007/978-981-95-1287-4_7. Original source: W.M. Robertson, Hydrogen permeation, diffusion and solution in nickel, Z. Metallkd. (Int. J. Mater. Res.) 64 (1973) 436-443. Range 300-775 K as Steward (1983, UCRL-53441, Table 5) gives for this paper's permeability; the diffusivity is from the same measurements. Converted from the printed row. Table 7.2 heads the column m2 s-1 and kJ/mol, but this row is printed in cgs and calorie units: D0 = (4.02 +/- 0.37) x 10^-3 cm2/s = (4.02 +/- 0.37) x 10^-7 m2/s, and Ea = 9.39 +/- 0.08 kcal/mol = 39.29 +/- 0.33 kJ/mol. The energy matches the row's permeability energy (13.09 kcal/mol = 54.8 kJ/mol) less the heat of solution, and the result is close to other nickel diffusivities (about 7 x 10^-7 m2/s, 40 kJ/mol).
